rules: A knowledge short told by a narrator over motion graphics: one surprising idea, explained so a 12-year-old gets it on first watch, ending in a payoff the viewer wants to repeat to a friend.
Beat 1 is the hook: the most surprising claim or number, spoken in under 3 seconds, with an on-screen text card of 7 words or fewer.
Every beat shows something: beats[].action names the number, comparison, scale, chart, steps or picture the graphic shows, with real values and units.

Every fact and number is true and the arithmetic checks out; round honestly and say 'about' when you round. When the premise is a thought experiment, say what really happens (the real-world limit or record).
Escalate: each beat makes the idea bigger or turns it; the last third lands the payoff, then one line loops back to the hook or asks the viewer a question.
The narrator carries it. Library characters may appear in a beat or two as an example or a reaction, never required; cast may be empty.
About 10 spoken characters per second: 550 characters is about a minute. Short sentences, one idea each.
In every line wrap 1-3 key words in *asterisks* (they render highlighted). No emoji.

rubric.check: Every number, unit and fact is correct, the arithmetic checks out, rounding is honest, and a thought experiment says what really happens.
Every beat names a concrete visual (a number, comparison, scale, chart, list or picture) that carries its point with the sound off.
A 12-year-old follows it on first watch: one idea, no unexplained jargon, comparisons to familiar things.
The payoff is a fact the viewer would repeat to a friend.
